what: VF Corporation owns outdoor and casual clothing brands: Vans, The North Face, Timberland and Dickies, sold through its own stores, its websites and wholesale retailers.
customers: Consumers buying outdoor and lifestyle clothing and footwear worldwide.
moat: Brands with decades of recognition in specific subcultures, which is why they can be revived even after a period of mismanagement.
risks: Vans has been in decline for years and the turnaround is unproven
Revenue fell from $11.8B to $9.6B over four years
$5.0B of debt against $824M of cash after years of over-distribution
opportunities: 11.4 times free cash flow with $691M of free cash flow
The North Face keeps growing and is now the largest brand, partly offsetting Vans
New management has cut costs, sold non-core brands and is paying down debt
watch: Vans revenue trend, which is the whole turnaround question.
